title: U.S. House · New York's 12th Congressional District
area: Manhattan's West Side, East Side, and Midtown, including the Upper West Side, Upper East Side, and Midtown Manhattan.

context.text: This is an open seat: incumbent Rep. Jerrold Nadler did not seek re-election in 2026.

Micah Lasher won a crowded eight-way Democratic primary on June 23, 2026 with 38.9% of the vote (41,940 votes), defeating Alex Bores (34.9%), Jack Schlossberg (10.9%), Nina Schwalbe (7.2%), George Conway (6.1%), Laura Dunn (1.4%), Patrick Timmins (0.3%), and Christopher Diep (0.2%).
Caroline Shinkle advanced unopposed as the Republican and Conservative Party nominee after both primaries were canceled.
Robb Huhn and Lucian Wintrich, who had been circulating as independent candidates, are listed by Ballotpedia as withdrawn or disqualified and are not on the November 3 general-election ballot.

candidates.name: Micah Lasher
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 23 Democratic primary in an eight-candidate field
candidates.currentRole: New York State Assembly member, District 69 (since 2025)

priorities.text: Says Democrats in Congress need to use every procedural tool available to oppose the Trump administration and, if Democrats retake the House, pursue aggressive oversight of ICE, tariffs, and the Justice Department.
Wants to expand federal investment in child care and housing tax credits, and to raise the federal minimum wage and index it to inflation.
Says immigration enforcement under the Trump administration has denied due process to immigrants and wants Congress to support the Restoring Access to Detainees Act and other due-process protections.
Says incumbent Democrats have not done enough to fight the Trump administration's agenda and that his campaign is about bringing more fight to Washington.
priorities.quote: What's it going to take to stop Donald Trump and his sycophants in Congress? A whole lot more fight and vision than we've seen from Democrats in Washington....I'm running for Congress to change that. It's time to start using every lever of power we have to fight back.

positions.summary: Campaign platform lists Medicare for All among his priorities, alongside opposition to Republican-led cuts to the Affordable Care Act.
positions.quote: repeal Trump's tax breaks for the rich, pass Medicare for All, raise the minimum wage, massively expand childcare, replace the crazy tariffs with policies that protect American workers

positions.summary: Wants to repeal the 2017 Trump tax cuts for high earners and says billionaires should pay more.

Opposes the Trump administration's broad tariffs, saying they raise costs for consumers and businesses, and wrote a state Tariff Transparency Act as an Assembly member to disclose tariffs' effect on automobile prices.
Supports abolishing ICE in its current form and backs the Restoring Access to Detainees Act to guarantee due process, access to lawyers, and family contact for detained immigrants.
Wants to raise the federal minimum wage and index it to inflation, following work in the Assembly to index New York's minimum wage.
Wants to expand housing tax credits, increase rental assistance funding, and use federal dollars to spur pro-housing state and local policy.

Served on the board of national gun-safety group Everytown and, according to his campaign, played a leading role in writing New York's gun-safety laws passed after the Buffalo and Uvalde mass shootings.

record.text: As a New York State Assembly member, sponsored legislation empowering the state Attorney General to take up enforcement work of federal agencies (such as the CFPB, FTC, and DOJ) that are shut down or restricted by the Trump administration.
Introduced a state constitutional amendment that would allow New York to redraw its congressional district lines mid-decade if another state redraws its lines first.

Wrote New York's RECOURSE Act, allowing the state to withhold funds it owes the federal government if the federal government illegally withholds funds from New York, and the Tariff Transparency Act, requiring disclosure of tariffs' effect on automobile prices.
Wrote legislation to guarantee continued access to the COVID-19 vaccine in New York State; the proposal was incorporated into Governor Hochul's 2026 budget.

Sponsored legislation to protect tenants and create the state's first public revolving loan fund for mixed-income housing, and wrote the Consumer Grocery Pricing Fairness Act aimed at small and independent grocers.

As a senior state and city policy aide before his Assembly election, worked on New York's gun-safety laws passed after the Buffalo and Uvalde shootings, the state's post-Dobbs abortion-provider protection law, indexing the state minimum wage to inflation, and a $1 billion mental-health investment plan.

candidates.name: Caroline Shinkle
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced unopposed through the Republican and Conservative Party primaries

priorities.text: Says her top priority is letting New Yorkers keep more of what they earn by reducing taxes on work, increasing the housing supply, and pursuing deregulation.
Wants to revamp public education quality and affordability in the district.
Prioritizes public safety and says she will champion law enforcement and first responders.
Describes herself as running to give Manhattan voters "a real choice on the ballot" and to bring pro-growth, pro-business economic policy to the district.
priorities.quote: I am running for Congress to give voters in Manhattan a real choice on the ballot. It's time to resurrect the power of private enterprise and common-sense thinking and deliver tangible solutions to the outrageous cost of living in New York City.

positions.summary: Campaign priorities page calls for streamlining permitting, repurposing unused office space and upzoning near transit corridors to increase housing supply.
positions.quote: Repurpose unused office space, streamline permitting, and advocate for upzoning near transit corridors.

statements.quote: Empower parents with school choice and greater curriculum transparency
Lower the cost of living through increasing energy production and promoting an all-energy-options-on-the-table approach
Reintroduce competition into the healthcare marketplace and enhance price transparency to ensure the system works for patients and providers, not just the insurance companies

priorities.text: Wants to put people in charge of decisions about AI, data, and technology rather than leaving the rules to corporations, through what she calls a "Public Interest Technology Plan."
Wants to protect workers from exploitation, retaliation, and digital workplace surveillance as part of a "Dignity of Work" agenda.
Wants to expand federal support for affordable-housing preservation and lower costs for child care and elder care under a "Household Security Plan."
Wants to increase transparency about who profits from government decisions as part of a "Public Trust Plan" for clean government.

positions.summary: Platform calls for ending carried-interest tax treatment and tightening S-corporation rules.
positions.quote: End carried interest treatment, tighten S-corp loopholes, and require sunset reviews of major business tax breaks so corporate welfare earns its keep or expires

positions.summary: Platform calls for building toward universal coverage through a public baseline plan with automatic enrollment.
positions.quote: Build toward universal coverage through automatic enrollment in a public baseline plan, with the ability to keep employer coverage

positions.summary: Platform's foreign policy plan says tariffs should target specific violations rather than broadly.
positions.quote: Target the specific violation, not American households.

positions.summary: Platform says military force should require Congressional authorization.
positions.quote: No use of force without Article I authorization stating an end state, a cost estimate, and a trigger for admitting failure.

positions.summary: Platform calls for narrowing ICE enforcement to serious-threat cases and reducing mass detention.
positions.quote: Narrow ICE to genuine serious-threat cases; move routine civil cases to supervised legal processing instead of mass detention

statements.quote: Expand federal support for affordable housing preservation
statements.context: In her Household Security Plan on her campaign site

statements.quote: Establish a Family Care Credit that offsets the cost of licensed child care or in-home elder care for working families
statements.context: In her Household Security Plan on her campaign site

priorities.text: Says Congress has a duty to impeach and remove officials, including the president, who violate their oath of office, and pledges to introduce articles of impeachment against President Trump on her first day if elected.
Supports Medicare for All covering gender-affirming care, abortion, fertility treatment, vaccination, and dental care, saying healthcare should not be tied to employment.
Wants to end U.S. military aid to Israel and reduce the U.S. military's global footprint, redirecting spending toward domestic needs.

positions.summary: Supports Medicare for All, including coverage for gender-affirming care, abortion, fertility treatment, vaccination, and dental care.
Supports an arms embargo on Israel and an end to U.S. funding, saying American tax dollars should not fund the conflict in Gaza.
Says ICE has repeatedly violated due-process rights and should be abolished.
Supports abortion access without restriction as part of a Medicare for All healthcare platform.

researchNotes: Karen Ortiz has no independent biographical information available beyond her campaign platform (no Ballotpedia biography, LinkedIn, or news profile found); her entry reflects only her stated positions. Robb Huhn and Lucian Wintrich, who appear in the pre-primary candidate snapshot, are listed by Ballotpedia as withdrawn/disqualified from the general-election ballot and are not included. Caroline Shinkle: campaign priorities page re-read; added school choice, energy and health care statements. Her page does not state positions on abortion, guns, immigration enforcement or taxes on high earners. Wilneida Negron: re-read the full campaign site plans; replaced two earlier housing and child-care 'positions' (which did not take a side on the guide's statements) with statements, and added tax, health coverage, tariffs, war powers and immigration-enforcement positions with verbatim quotes. The site does not address abortion, guns, rent regulation or the minimum wage as a specific figure. Biographical detail for Wilneida Negrón and Karen Ortiz comes largely from their own campaign materials and Ballotpedia Candidate Connection profiles; no independent news profiles were found, and employers and dates for Negrón's career are not specified in those materials.
